**A TRIP'S LIVE ACTIVITY IS PUSH-TO-START, which is the whole reason this endpoint exists and is shaped differently from §7.21's per-ride registration.** A leg begins when the CAR sets off — an event the phone learns about from a push, while the app is very likely not running — and **ActivityKit does not let a background app start an Activity.** So the app registers a push-to-start token up front, once per trip, and the **server** starts the Activity when the leg begins. **§7.21's token addresses one already-started Activity; this one addresses the CAPABILITY to start them.**

**The OWNER may register too, by explicit product decision** — the owner is included in the per-leg Activity — so the route is open to anybody the store admits to the trip.

##### Request

```http
POST /api/trips/cltrip0001/activity-start-token HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Content-Type: application/json

{ "pushToStartToken": "<opaque ActivityKit token>", "sandbox": false }
```

`pushToStartToken` is **1 to 256 characters**; anything else is `400` naming the FIELD and never the VALUE. `sandbox` names the APNs gateway — a development or TestFlight build mints a sandbox token and pushing it to production is rejected as `BadDeviceToken` — and is carried **per registration** rather than read from the device registry, because **starting an Activity needs no notification permission and the user may have no device row at all.** Absent means production, matching §7.21.

##### Response — 204 No Content

**UPSERT, NOT INSERT, because ActivityKit ROTATES the push-to-start token.** A re-registration replaces the value in place; accumulating rows would mean two starts on one phone for one leg — two Live Activities for the same journey on the same lock screen.

**THE MEMBERSHIP READ IS THE GATE.** Registering a token is granting the server permission to write to this phone's lock screen about this trip, so it has to be a trip the caller is actually on. The read answers `404` for everybody else, so the endpoint is not an oracle for trip ids either.

**THE TOKEN IS P1 AND A CAPABILITY.** Whoever holds it together with the team's APNs signing key can start a Live Activity on that phone. It is **never echoed in a response, never placed in an error message, and not logged on this path at all**. The `204` carries **no body**, which is the strongest form of *"the caller already knows what they sent"* — echoing it would only put it in every client log and proxy trace.

#### 7.30.9 `DELETE /api/trips/{tripId}/activity-start-token` — clear it

> **Anchored:** FR-9.3, NFR-3.21. Contracts **v0.41.0**. No request body, no response body. Implemented by [MYR-602](https://linear.app/myrobotaxi/issue/MYR-602).

##### Response — 204 No Content, IDEMPOTENT

No row removed is the same answer as one row removed.

**⚠ NO MEMBERSHIP READ, UNLIKE THE `POST`, AND THE ASYMMETRY IS DELIBERATE.** This operation only ever deletes **the caller's own row**, keyed `(trip_id, user_id)` on the authenticated subject. The worst a stranger can achieve is deleting a row they do not have. Requiring a read would add a `404` that tells them whether the trip is real, for a call that changes nothing either way — a strictly worse trade than the one §7.30.8 makes, where the read gates a real capability grant.

**And it would break the case the endpoint most needs to serve: a participant who has just LEFT must still be able to clear their token — and after leaving they no longer pass the membership read.** A registration that could be created and not withdrawn is a lock-screen capability with no off switch.

#### 7.30.10 `DELETE /api/trips/{tripId}` — the owner deletes a trip

> **Anchored:** FR-5.3, NFR-3.21. Contracts **v0.41.0** — **no schema change, no new error code, no new push event, no migration**. No request body, no response body. Implemented by [MYR-607](https://linear.app/myrobotaxi/issue/MYR-607) (client-directed: *"have the ability to delete the trip at anytime"*).

##### Purpose

The owner removes a trip entirely: the window, the roster, the legs and the Live Activity registrations. **Owner only; `404` to everybody else, including a participant.** It is the tenth route on this surface and the only one that removes a trip rather than changing it.

##### It is allowed in EVERY status, and that is deliberate

**Scheduled, active and `ended` trips are all deletable.** §7.30.4 refuses to MUTATE a finished window with `409 conflict / trip_ended`, and the two rules do not conflict: **that refusal is about extending `endsAt`, which would resurrect live access every participant was already told had ended.** A deletion grants nothing to anybody — it is the only mutation on this surface that can only ever *reduce* what people can see — so the same refusal here would strand finished trips on people's lists forever, which is precisely the case the owner most often means.

##### Response — 204 No Content

**No body.** There is nothing left to describe, and returning the trip's last state would invite a cache to keep it.

**A SECOND CALL IS `404`, and a client MUST read that as done.** The store finds no row and answers with the same sentinel a stranger gets. From the client's side that is indistinguishable from success and is meant to be: **a delete that answered `404` on the retry of its own timed-out request would be a bug the app could not tell from a bug in the server.**

##### What is deleted, and what is not

**Four tables, one transaction, child-first:**

| Removed | |
|---|---|
| `go_live_activities` rows anchored to this trip's legs | the participants' and owner's running **leg cards** |
| `go_trip_legs` | every leg the car drove inside the window |
| `go_trip_activity_tokens` | every party's ActivityKit **push-to-start** registration for this trip |
| `go_trip_participants` | the roster — a **hard delete**, unlike §7.30.6's `left_at` tombstone, because after the trip is gone there is no trip for *"was this person ever on it"* to be about |
| `go_trips` | the window itself, guarded `WHERE id = $1 AND owner_user_id = $2` |

**⚠ THE VEHICLE'S DRIVES ARE UNTOUCHED, and that is the sentence the confirm dialog puts in front of the owner.** A trip never OWNED a drive — the window merely **selected** one, by time, from the car's own history (§7.30.7) — so deleting the window deletes the *selection* and nothing else. Nothing else on the platform moves either: the shares are untouched (a trip creates no relationship, so deleting one destroys none), and other trips on the same car are untouched.

The statements are explicit even though migration **0047**'s foreign keys would cascade all four from the parent alone. `go_live_activities` is reached only THROUGH `go_trip_legs`, so the cascade that covers it is **two links long** — and a two-link cascade is invisible at the call site, while the row it silently missed would be a live capability addressed at somebody's lock screen.

##### End, settle, delete — and the order is normative

**Three steps, in this order:** `endedAt` is stamped (the §7.30.5 statement, reused — owner-scoped, guarded on `ended_at IS NULL`, so a no-op on a trip that has already ended); the trip is settled (every open leg ended, every party's leg Live Activity ended, `trip_ended` fanned out, the WebSocket re-mask nudged — `trips.Service`'s `SettleTrip` machinery under a second name, so a deletion and an ordinary closing edge do the same work through the same code); the rows are removed.

**SETTLE BEFORE DELETE, because everything the settlement does reads rows the delete is about to remove:** who is on the trip, which leg is open, which device holds which card. Run the other way round, a participant's lock screen would keep a live Activity for a journey that no longer exists, addressed by a token nothing can look up any more, until ActivityKit's own staleness ceiling retired it hours later.

**END BEFORE SETTLE, and that step exists ONLY for the half-done state** — on the happy path the row is deleted a moment later and nothing ever reads the stamp. The settlement takes every card down and tells every participant the trip is over. **Without `endedAt` written first, a delete that then FAILED would leave the trip ACTIVE, so those people would keep the car's live location for the rest of a window they had just been told had closed** — told it ended, still watching. With it, the trip is genuinely over, the client's retry deletes it, and the only artefact is a trip that reads as `ended` on the owner's own list until then. **That is the conservative direction**, and it is the one the reverse ordering cannot offer: its failure is a stranded card on somebody else's phone that nothing can clear.

##### The push: `trip_ended` with `deleted: true`

**A deletion sends `trip_ended` carrying `"deleted": true` — a JSON boolean, present only on a deletion and absent (never `false`) on an ordinary end.** See §7.19.5.

**IT IS NOT A SIXTH `trips` EVENT, and that is a contract decision.** Every installed build switches on `event`, and a value they have never seen routes to their default arm — which for a lifecycle push is *do nothing* — so a deleted trip would silently stay on the phone of exactly the people it was deleted out from under. `trip_ended` is already the sentence they act on (*the window is over, drop the live card*); `deleted` only tells a build that KNOWS about it to go one step further and remove the trip from the list rather than leaving an ended one behind.

**Participants only, never the owner** — the same self-suppression the other four events use: the owner pressed the button.

**Sent only when the trip was `scheduled` or `active`.** Deleting last month's trips must not put a banner on anybody's phone; they were told it ended when it ended. Two guards enforce it, belt and braces exactly as on §7.30.5: the handler's status gate answers for a trip that was already over when the request arrived, and the `ended_notified_at` claim answers for one that ended WHILE the request was in flight — an owner tapping End and Delete in the same second settles once and announces once.

##### Access, and when it actually stops

Live access ends when the rows do: `internal/auth`'s fourth UNION leg joins `go_trips` and `go_trip_participants`, so a deleted trip grants nothing on the next lookup. **A connected socket is re-masked to `viewer` by the `AccessRevalidator`'s own 60-second tick**, not by the nudge this route fires — the nudge is asked for while the rows still exist, so what it observes is the state before the delete. That is the same mechanism, for the same reason, as a window that lapses on the clock ([`trips.md`](../architecture/trips.md) §10): a trip edge has no mutation for a revocation nudge to hang off, so the tick is not a backstop but THE mechanism.

##### Audit

**One `trip.deleted` AuditLog row, written INSIDE the deletion transaction and BEFORE the deletes** (CG-DL-3). `targetType='trip'`, `targetId`=the trip's cuid, `userId`=the owner, `initiator='user'`, `metadata={vehicleId}` — **two opaque cuids across the whole row and nothing else** (CG-DL-5). No trip NAME (P1 user content sealed at rest, [`data-classification.md`](data-classification.md) §1.25) and no participant list: who was on somebody's road trip is a fact about those people, and they are not the subject of this row. **It is the only record the participants have** — everything else about the window is gone. See [`data-lifecycle.md`](data-lifecycle.md) §4.2 and §3.6.

##### Errors

The shared table below. `404` for an unknown id, a trip the caller does not own, and one they are only a participant of — **one answer, never `403`**. `503` when `TRIPS_ENABLED=false`, like every other route here. `500` on a store failure, which is the case the settle-first ordering makes visible.

#### 7.30.11 `GET /api/trips/{tripId}/addable-people` — who is still addable

> **Anchored:** FR-5.1, FR-5.4, NFR-3.21. Contracts **v0.41.0 + the MYR-618 additions** — `TripAddablePerson` and the `TripAddablePeopleResponse` envelope are NEW shapes and `TripParticipant.addedByName` is a NEW optional field, both additive, both vendored into this repo's copy of [`trip.schema.json`](schemas/trip.schema.json) ahead of the upstream tag in `myrobotaxi/contracts`. **No new top-level error code, no new sub-code, one Go-owned migration (0060).** No request body; response [`trip.schema.json#/$defs/TripAddablePeopleResponse`](schemas/trip.schema.json). Implemented by [MYR-618](https://linear.app/myrobotaxi/issue/MYR-618) (client-directed: *"add the ability for anyone in the group to add someone to the trip as long as they have access to the car already"*).

##### Purpose

The picker behind §7.30.4's add: **the trip vehicle's accepted, unsuspended grant-holders who are not already on this trip.** Admitted to the owner **and to live participants** — `404` to everyone else, like every other per-trip route.

**IT EXISTS BECAUSE §7.5's GRANT LISTING IS OWNER-ONLY AND MUST STAY THAT WAY.** A participant who may add people needs to know who is addable, and the owner's own share list is the wrong place to get it: it carries invite codes, email addresses, pending invitations, per-grant permissions and the owner's private memo about why each person has a key. This returns **a name and an id**, for people who already hold a live grant on the car, minus the ones already aboard — the minimum a picker needs and nothing a picker does not.

**THE OWNER READS THE SAME ROUTE.** One list, built by one statement, so an owner's picker and a participant's picker cannot come to offer different people.

##### Request

```http
GET /api/trips/cltrip0001/addable-people HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer <token>
```

No query parameters. **No cursor, and no pagination** — the same envelope decision §7.30.2 makes: a car has a handful of share-holders, not a feed, and an SDK pagination helper MUST NOT mistake this for a page and go looking for a cursor that will never be there.

##### Response — 200 OK

```json
{
  "people": [
    { "shareId": "clshare0003", "displayName": "Joey" },
    { "shareId": "clshare0004", "displayName": "Mom" }
  ]
}
```

| Field | Type | Classification | Notes |
|-------|------|----------------|-------|
| `people[]` | array | P1 (names) | **EMPTY RATHER THAN ABSENT** when everybody with access is already aboard, and `200` rather than `404` — "there is nobody left to add" is a legitimate state of a trip the caller is on, and the client renders *"Everyone with access to {car} is already on this trip."* |
| `shareId` | `string` | P0 | The GRANT's id — **the same value the roster calls `participantId` and `PATCH` calls `addParticipantIds`**, so a picked person round-trips into the add with no translation and no mapping table on the client. Opaque; consumers MUST NOT parse it or assume it survives a revoke-and-reinvite |
| `displayName` | `string` | **P1** | The accepting account's **confirmed FIRST name**, else the owner's own label for the grant — the identical ladder, fallback and first-name-only policy as `participants[].name`, so a person cannot be called one thing in the picker and another thing on the trip they were added to one tap later. **NO CODE, NO EMAIL, NO STATUS, NO PERMISSION, NO USER ID** |

**Ordered by `displayName`, with the share id as a total tie-break**, so a picker showing two people the owner labelled the same does not reshuffle them between reads.

##### The predicate, stated once

A person appears here when **all** of the following hold: they hold a share on the trip's vehicle; that share is `accepted`; it is **not suspended**; it has been redeemed by an account; that account is not the trip's owner; and they are **not on the trip's live roster**.

**⚠ IT CARRIES THE FULL LIVE-GRANT PREDICATE, not because a read grants anything, but because its rows are what a client posts straight back to §7.30.4.** A picker that offered a suspended grant would produce a `participant_not_shared` refusal the person could not explain, having just been shown the name.

**SOMEBODY WHO LEFT THE TRIP IS OFFERED AGAIN** — the roster exclusion tests `left_at IS NULL` — which is what makes a re-invite possible after a departure. The OWNER never appears: they hold no grant on their own car.

##### Errors

The shared table below. **`404` for an unknown trip id, a trip the caller is not on, and one they have left — one answer, never `403`.** The membership probe is what makes that true: the list statement returns no rows for a stranger anyway, but **an empty list is also the honest answer for a trip where everybody is aboard**, so without the probe the two would be indistinguishable and a stranger would receive `200`. `503` when `TRIPS_ENABLED=false`.

##### Errors — one table for all eleven routes

**ONE MAPPING FOR EVERY TRIP ENDPOINT**, so the same condition cannot answer `409` on one route and `400` on another — which is the drift that makes a client's error handling a per-endpoint special case.

| HTTP | `error.code` | `subCode` | When |
|------|--------------|-----------|------|
| 400 | `invalid_request` | — | A malformed or unparseable body; **any unknown field** (strict decode); a body over 16 KiB; `startsAt`/`endsAt` not RFC 3339 (the refusal names the field); a window that is empty, inverted or longer than 30 days; an `endsAt` in the past on `PATCH` (**end the trip instead**); a name empty after trimming, over 60 **runes**, or carrying a control character; `?status=` not one of `scheduled`/`active`/`ended`; `?limit=` not an integer in [1, 100]; a malformed `?cursor=`; `pushToStartToken` empty or over 256 characters; a missing `{vehicleId}` or `{tripId}` path value |
| 400 | `invalid_request` | `participant_not_shared` | One or more requested participants is **not a live accepted, unsuspended share-holder on this vehicle** (§7.30.1 create, §7.30.4 add). **DELIBERATELY UNSPECIFIC ABOUT WHICH ONE, AND ABOUT WHY** — "no such share", "a share on a different car", "an invite never redeemed" and "a suspended grant" are one answer, because naming the failing id would make the endpoint an oracle for other people's share ids. The client's action is the same in all four cases: re-fetch the roster and let the owner pick again |
| 401 | `auth_failed` | — | Missing `Authorization` header, or an invalid/expired bearer |
| 403 | `vehicle_not_owned` | — | **§7.30.1 ONLY.** The caller does not own the vehicle they tried to open a window on. See the 404-not-403 rule for why CREATE is the exception |
| 403 | `permission_denied` | — | **§7.30.4 ONLY.** A LIVE PARTICIPANT sent a body carrying `removeParticipantIds`, `name` or `endsAt` — verbs that stay with the owner ([MYR-618](https://linear.app/myrobotaxi/issue/MYR-618)). **The whole request is refused and NOTHING is applied**, even when a legal `addParticipantIds` rode alongside. `403` rather than `404` because this caller's membership is not in doubt — they can read the trip through the same handler — so there is nothing left to conceal, and the message names the VERBS rather than the field: the client's fix is to stop offering the button, not to rename a key |
| 404 | `not_found` | — | **An unknown trip id AND a trip the caller is not on — ONE answer, deliberately** (unknown, somebody else's, or one the caller has left). Also an unknown `{vehicleId}` on §7.30.1, and a trip the caller only PARTICIPATES in on §7.30.10. **Since [MYR-618](https://linear.app/myrobotaxi/issue/MYR-618) a participant is NOT `404` on §7.30.4** — they may add people, and a body reaching for an owner's verb is answered `403 permission_denied` instead, because their membership is not in doubt. **A client MUST NOT read `404` here as "this trip does not exist"**; it means *"there is no trip here that you may act on"* — and on §7.30.10 specifically, a `404` on a retry means **the delete already succeeded** |
| 409 | `conflict` | `trip_overlaps` | Another **scheduled-or-active** trip on the same vehicle already covers part of the requested window (§7.30.1, and §7.30.4 when `endsAt` moves). It earns a sub-code because the client's next move is specific and not derivable from `conflict` alone: send the owner back to the **date picker**, knowing that the CAR — not the trip, not the participants — is what is double-booked. The same reasoning that gave `time_conflict` its own sub-code on §7.8 |
| 409 | `conflict` | `trip_ended` | A mutation of a trip whose window has already closed (§7.30.4). A bare `conflict` on a trip the owner is looking at right now is indistinguishable from a server bug and the client would retry; with this it can say the true thing — **the trip is over, start a new one** — which is also the only thing that would work |
| 500 | `internal_error` | — | A store-layer failure. **Includes §7.30.6**, whose `204` is the answer to "you are not on this trip" and never to "the database is down" |
| 503 | `service_unavailable` | — | `TRIPS_ENABLED=false`. **Every route, reads included**, checked **before** authentication. `503` and never `404` — see the kill-switch block |

**EVERY REFUSAL RIDES AN EXISTING TOP-LEVEL CODE (§4.1.1).** `wserrors.ErrorCode` is a CLOSED enum the SDKs decode into a generated union, so a new member is a five-file change across two repos and a breaking decode on every shipped client that has not been rebuilt. Trips needed none: the refusals are an illegal state (`conflict`), a bad body (`invalid_request`), two denials (`vehicle_not_owned` on CREATE, and since [MYR-618](https://linear.app/myrobotaxi/issue/MYR-618) `permission_denied` on the participant branch of §7.30.4), an absence (`not_found`) and a disabled feature (`service_unavailable`) — things the vocabulary already says.

**WHAT IS NEW IS THREE SUB-CODES**, which is the mechanism that exists exactly for this: telling a client WHICH conflict, when the primary code alone does not say what to do next. `subCode` is an **open string** on `ws-messages.schema.json` — the enum is documented in prose, not declared — so emitting a new value is schema-**VALID** today and needs no client rebuild. Contracts v0.41.0 does not yet list these three in that prose enum; the values match the spec's own wording so the upstream addition is a documentation change rather than a rename. **Catalogued as DV-26 (§10).**

**Error MESSAGES carry no user content.** The trip NAME is P1 and never appears in an error, a log line or a `500`'s text — an error path is the one place a value reliably reaches a log without anybody deciding it should. Log lines identify a trip by its cuid (P0).

#### Implementation

Handlers: [`internal/telemetry/trip_handler.go`](../../internal/telemetry/trip_handler.go) (create, list, the shared preamble and the error writer), [`trip_detail_handler.go`](../../internal/telemetry/trip_detail_handler.go) (get, patch, end, leave), [`trip_roster_handler.go`](../../internal/telemetry/trip_roster_handler.go) (MYR-618's participant branch of §7.30.4 and §7.30.11), [`trip_delete_handler.go`](../../internal/telemetry/trip_delete_handler.go) (§7.30.10), [`trip_drives_handler.go`](../../internal/telemetry/trip_drives_handler.go), [`trip_activity_token_handler.go`](../../internal/telemetry/trip_activity_token_handler.go), with the wire projection in [`trip_wire.go`](../../internal/telemetry/trip_wire.go) and the error map in [`trip_errors.go`](../../internal/telemetry/trip_errors.go). The §7.2/§7.3/§7.4 admission is [`trip_drive_access.go`](../../internal/telemetry/trip_drive_access.go); the catalog's third merge leg is [`vehicles_list_trip.go`](../../internal/telemetry/vehicles_list_trip.go). Store: `store.TripRepo` across [`trip_repo.go`](../../internal/store/trip_repo.go), [`trip_repo_read.go`](../../internal/store/trip_repo_read.go), [`trip_repo_write.go`](../../internal/store/trip_repo_write.go), [`trip_repo_delete.go`](../../internal/store/trip_repo_delete.go), [`trip_repo_drives.go`](../../internal/store/trip_repo_drives.go) and [`trip_repo_catalog.go`](../../internal/store/trip_repo_catalog.go), [`trip_repo_participants.go`](../../internal/store/trip_repo_participants.go) (MYR-618's add path and the addable-people read) and [`trip_added_by_name.go`](../../internal/store/trip_added_by_name.go), with every statement in [`trip_queries.go`](../../internal/store/trip_queries.go) so the authorization-relevant statement set can be read at once. Schema: migrations [`0047_trips.up.sql`](../../internal/store/migrations/0047_trips.up.sql) and [`0060_trip_participant_added_by.up.sql`](../../internal/store/migrations/0060_trip_participant_added_by.up.sql) (the roster's `added_by_user_id`, **nullable and deliberately not backfilled** — every pre-MYR-618 row was written by the owner, and a backfill would record, indistinguishably from a real observation, an act nobody observed). Role resolution: [`internal/auth/vehicle_access.go`](../../internal/auth/vehicle_access.go) and [`queries.go`](../../internal/auth/queries.go)'s fourth UNION leg. Field masks: [`internal/mask/tables.go`](../../internal/mask/tables.go) and [`sentinels.go`](../../internal/mask/sentinels.go).

**Not in [`specs/rest.openapi.yaml`](specs/rest.openapi.yaml)**, on §7.23's and §7.29's reasoning: that spec declares only the core read and sharing subset. This surface's canonical machine-readable shape is [`schemas/trip.schema.json`](schemas/trip.schema.json).

**THE LIVE HALF IS `internal/trips`**: the window sweeper (the boundary `trip_started` / `trip_ended` pushes and their at-most-once stamps), the leg detector that writes `go_trip_legs`, the per-leg Live Activity **push-to-start** fan-out (§7.21.7), the `trips` push **category** and its §7.19 prefs toggle, and the WebSocket revalidator's **re-mask**. **The seam between the two is `telemetry.TripNotifier`** ([`trip_notifier.go`](../../internal/telemetry/trip_notifier.go)), satisfied at composition by an adapter over `trips.Service`: **nil is a no-op, not a failure** — a deployment with no notifier creates trips that work perfectly and tells nobody, because a push is an announcement about a state change and never the state change itself. The owner's early end reaches `SettleTrip` through the same seam, which is why a closing edge ends the open leg's card BEFORE the banner. See [`docs/architecture/trips.md`](../architecture/trips.md) §12.

## 8. Resource schemas

The canonical v1 `VehicleState` schema is [`schemas/vehicle-state.schema.json`](schemas/vehicle-state.schema.json). The REST snapshot endpoint returns that shape directly via `$ref` in the OpenAPI spec -- it is NOT re-declared.

REST-only resource shapes are declared inline in [`specs/rest.openapi.yaml`](specs/rest.openapi.yaml) under `components/schemas` for v1. The following shapes are defined there:

| Schema | Used by | Notes |
|--------|---------|-------|
| `DriveSummary` | `GET /api/vehicles/{vehicleId}/drives` item | Subset of FR-3.4 for list rendering. |
| `DriveDetail` | `GET /api/drives/{driveId}` response | Full FR-3.4 record minus `routePoints`. |
| `DriveRoute` | `GET /api/drives/{driveId}/route` response | `{driveId, routePoints[]}`. |
| `RoutePoint` | `DriveRoute.routePoints[]` item | `{lat, lng, speed, heading, timestamp}` matching `RoutePointRecord` from [`data-classification.md`](data-classification.md) §1.5. |
| `Invite` | All three invite endpoints | Full row from `data-classification.md` §1.6. |
| `CreateInviteRequest` | `POST /api/vehicles/{vehicleId}/invites` request body | `{label, email, permission}`. |
| `ErrorEnvelope` | All non-2xx responses | `{error: {code, message, subCode?}}`. |
| `PaginatedDrives` | `GET /api/vehicles/{vehicleId}/drives` response | `{items, nextCursor, hasMore}` wrapper. |
| `PaginatedInvites` | `GET /api/vehicles/{vehicleId}/invites` response | `{items}` without cursor (unpaginated in v1). |
| `DeleteUserResponse` | `DELETE /api/users/me` response | `{deleted, auditLogId}`. |

Every field in every inline schema carries an `x-classification` annotation (P0, P1, P2, or `mixed`) matching the convention in `schemas/ws-messages.schema.json` and `vehicle-state.schema.json`. This is non-negotiable -- `contract-guard` CG-DC-1 runs against these shapes too.

A follow-up issue (to be filed by DV-23's resolver) will extract these shapes to sibling JSON Schemas under `schemas/` so they can be `$ref`'d by both the OpenAPI spec and any future SDK code generator without embedding them in the YAML. The v1 scope keeps them inline to ship MYR-12 tightly.

## 9. Observability

> **Anchored:** FR-11.x (SDK side; REST endpoints share the same emission points as the WS surface).

REST endpoints emit the same slog / Prometheus / OpenTelemetry signals as the WebSocket surface. The existing `requestLogger` middleware in [`internal/server/middleware.go`](../../internal/server/middleware.go) already records `method`, `path`, `status`, `duration`, and `remote_addr` on every request; this is the emission point for REST observability. Additional middleware hooks PLANNED as part of the REST handler implementation (DV-19):

| Signal | Type | Labels / attributes | Notes |
|--------|------|---------------------|-------|
| `http_requests_total` | counter | `method`, `path_template`, `status_class`, `role` | Prometheus counter. `path_template` is the pattern (e.g., `/api/vehicles/:id/snapshot`), not the concrete path, to avoid cardinality explosion. `role` is `owner`, `viewer`, or `unauthenticated`. |
| `http_request_duration_seconds` | histogram | same | Prometheus histogram. SLO targets derive from `requirements.md` §3.1 latency table. |
| `http_errors_total` | counter | `method`, `path_template`, `error_code` | Cardinality bounded by the error code enum in §4.1.1. |
| slog `http request` | structured log | `method`, `path`, `status`, `duration`, `remote_addr`, `user_id`, `request_id`, `role` | Existing emission, extended to include `user_id`, `request_id`, and `role` after auth middleware resolves them. `user_id` is P0 (opaque cuid). NEVER log the `Authorization` header or any P1 field. |
| OTel span | trace | `http.method`, `http.route`, `http.status_code`, `user.id`, `vehicle.id` | W3C Trace Context propagated via the `traceparent` header. |

`contract-guard` Rule CG-DC-2 blocks any PR that introduces P1 values into log fields, error messages, or metric labels. The `vehicleId` / `driveId` / `userId` / `inviteId` IDs are P0 and are log-safe; the underlying sensitive values (GPS, addresses, tokens, emails) are P1 and MUST NOT appear in any observability output.

Every entry has a proposed Linear follow-up title. `contract-guard` treats any un-catalogued divergence as a failing contract violation. The divergence IDs (DV-NN) are stable -- new divergences take the next free number; closed divergences retain their ID in the change log. Divergence IDs DV-01 through DV-18 are owned by [`websocket-protocol.md`](websocket-protocol.md) §10; MYR-12 adds DV-19 through DV-23.

Same as [`websocket-protocol.md`](websocket-protocol.md) §10 divergence management rules (one-way door, closing rules, RESOLVED-with-implementation-pending, amendment divergences). a stranger still gets `404`, from the read. **THE PREDICATE DOES NOT SOFTEN**: a suspended grant is the same `400 participant_not_shared` for either caller (a `409` was considered and rejected — one condition must not answer two ways depending on who asked). **NEW §7.30.11 `GET /api/trips/{tripId}/addable-people`** — `{people:[{shareId, displayName}]}`, admitted to the owner AND to live participants, because §7.5's grant listing is owner-only and must stay that way: it carries invite CODES, email addresses, statuses, permissions and the owner's private label. **Names and ids only**; an empty array is a `200` (everybody is aboard) and a stranger is `404` — the membership probe is what makes those distinguishable. **ATTRIBUTION IS A COLUMN AND A ROW, not substitutes**: `go_trip_participants.added_by_user_id` (migration 0060, **nullable and deliberately NOT backfilled** — every pre-MYR-618 row was written by the owner, and a backfill would record an act nobody observed) feeds `addedByName` on every roster row, resolved through the same three-rung ladder and MYR-583 confirmation gate as `ownerFirstName`; the share id already names them to anybody entitled to ask). **⚠ THE UPSERT PRESERVES AN EXISTING ATTRIBUTION** and overwrites only on a genuine revival — without that, any participant could claim credit for the owner's own additions by re-adding the same person. **ONE NEW PUSH, `trip_participant_added` (§7.19.5), SIXTH EVENT ON THE EXISTING CATEGORY WITH NO NEW PREFERENCE**, and **the owner is its whole audience**: it is the one thing on the platform that changes who may watch an owner's car without the owner acting. The owner's OWN add sends it to nobody. Its two names ride the **sentence**, never `userInfo`; several additions are COUNTED, not listed; the trip's own name is in neither. **A separate store entry point rather than a flag on the owner's patch** — `AddParticipants` can only ever widen a roster because widening is the only statement it contains, while `Update` can rename, re-window and REMOVE. **Sections updated:** §6 (PATCH row + one new row), §7.19.5 (six events, the new row, the payload rule), §7.30 (ten routes → eleven, the kill switch, the error table's `404` and the new `403 permission_denied` row, the implementation paragraph), §7.30.3 (`addedByName`), §7.30.4 (rewritten: who may send what, the audit block), **§7.30.11 (new)**. [`data-lifecycle.md`](data-lifecycle.md): §4.2 (`trip.participant_added` action, the `trip` targetType). [`trips.md`](../architecture/trips.md): **§10B (new)**. | 2026-09-06 | **A trip is a time window, and for its length the people you picked can see the car ([MYR-602](https://linear.app/myrobotaxi/issue/MYR-602), CLIENT-DIRECTED: *"you should really only see live location during an active trip shared with a user"*).** Contracts **v0.41.0** — **nine new endpoints, one new schema file, one new OPTIONAL `VehicleSummary` field, three new sub-codes, ONE Go-owned migration, no new top-level error code, and a NARROWING that touches every installed client.** **THE NARROWING IS THE HEADLINE, not the endpoints.** A standing accepted share (MYR-184) used to carry the whole location group and the whole navigation group on the streaming path plus `VehicleSummary.location` on the catalog. This **supersedes MYR-435's** decision to keep navigation on a viewer: that argument was about a party watching a journey, and the client's position is that a durable remote share is not that party. **THE SENTINEL SUBSTITUTION (§5.1.1) IS THE PART A CONSUMER MUST READ.** Six of the withheld fields (`speed`, `heading`, `latitude`, `longitude`, `locationName`, `locationAddress`) are in `vehicle-state.schema.json`'s `required` array, which v0.41.0 did NOT relax — so removing them would not narrow the frame, it would make it **undecodable** for every installed build. Every OPTIONAL withheld field is still removed outright; `VehicleSummary.location`, being nullable and not required, is simply dropped. **THE SURFACE:** §7.30's nine routes on one handler — create (the ONE `403` here), list (**unpaginated**, `{items}` with no cursor), get, patch, end (idempotent, guarded on `ended_at IS NULL`), leave (**`204` always, silent**), the window's drives (**the first non-owner drive read on the platform**, §7.2 shape and cursor verbatim), and the ActivityKit **push-to-start** token pair. **Every per-trip route answers `404` to a caller who is not on the trip**, identically to an unknown id, because trip ids end up in deep links. **THE WINDOW:** `[startsAt, effectiveEnd)` with `effectiveEnd = min(endsAt, endedAt)`; `status` is **derived on every read and never stored** (a stored status is the one state the platform could not explain); a window **may start in the past**, which is how a road trip already driven joins a trip; 30-day cap; the drives bound is inclusive at both ends where the access predicate's upper bound is exclusive, and §7.30.7 says why. **ACCESS is a fourth UNION leg** in `internal/auth`, carrying three load-bearing predicates — the window, `left_at IS NULL`, and a **live-share join** that makes *"trip access can never outlive the share"* structural rather than a cleanup job. | 2026-09-05 | **Tesla will not let a DRIVER configure a car, and the card now says so ([MYR-599](https://linear.app/myrobotaxi/issue/MYR-599), review round).** Contracts **v0.40.0** — **one new `setupState` member, no new field, no new endpoint, no migration, no new error code, and two divergences CLOSED.** **THE UPSTREAM FACT, which is load-bearing and undocumented by Tesla.** `POST /api/1/vehicles/fleet_telemetry_config` is **OWNER-ONLY**: a token whose `access_type` for the VIN is `DRIVER` gets `404 {"error": "<VIN> not_found"}` while **that same token still lists the VIN** via `GET /api/1/vehicles` and can even `DELETE` its config. Visibility is not evidence of capability. Tesla's endpoint documentation enumerates only `missing_key` / `unsupported_hardware` / `unsupported_firmware` / `max_configs` and says nothing about owner vs driver, and `access_type` appears nowhere in the Fleet API docs at all; the restriction is established by Tesla staff on GitHub — collaborator **aaronpkahn** on [teslamotors/fleet-telemetry#116](https://github.com/teslamotors/fleet-telemetry/issues/116) (2024-03-14), answering *"only Owners can POST requests to `fleet_telemetry_config`"* with *"Good point. That is inconsistent behavior. We'll support DRIVER access on the POST endpoint soon"*, and the same person on [#126](https://github.com/teslamotors/fleet-telemetry/issues/126) the same day. **As of 2026-09-05 the announcements page carries no such entry, so the restriction is assumed to stand; whether Tesla shipped it silently is UNVERIFIED and only a real DRIVER token can settle it.** **WHAT WAS WRONG.** That 404 was recorded as `push_failed` — a **transient** label the derivation lets decay into `configuring` — so the very first thing a driver saw after consenting was a card reading *"connecting…"* about a car Tesla had refused outright, and the reconciler retried it forever against an answer that cannot change. **NEW `setupState` member `owner_access_required` on §7.0, §7.1, §7.23 and §7.29**, sorting **after `awaiting_owner_acknowledgment`** (the only state it can follow — the refusal is observable only on a push, and no push happens before consent is on record) and **before `awaiting_virtual_key` / `configuring` / `token_failed`** (a definitive refusal is not progress). **COPY MUST NOT SAY "RECONNECT TESLA"**: that is `token_failed`'s action, and here it sends a person round a loop that cannot end — the only thing that works is for the car's Tesla **owner** to add it under their own account and share it with the driver. **IT IS EMITTED ONLY ON POSITIVE EVIDENCE, because the 404 is generic** — a revoked grant returns the identical answer — so the driver cause is named only when the car carries an acknowledged `go_vehicle_driver_access` row, and a bare 404 still reports `token_failed`. The VIN-still-listed condition is established at LINK time, the only moment this server enumerates a fleet, and is deliberately not re-verified per push. **Before v0.40.0 this condition reported `token_failed`** — the only honest class the v0.39.0 enum offered, imprecise for the driver cause and never a fabricated progress state — so a client reading an older server sees that member for the same cars. **Server-side the refusal is a STATE AND NOT AN ERROR:** §7.23 and §7.29 answer `200` carrying it rather than `502`, because nothing failed on our side or on the request and a retry affordance would invite a retry that cannot succeed. The schedule records it on a **flat 24-hour** gap rather than a doubling ladder, and deliberately ignores the MYR-529 hot pairing epoch — pairing is not what is wrong, and hammering a refusal because somebody tapped unlock would be the wrong response to the right signal. **IT MAY STOP BEING TRUE WITHOUT ANY CHANGE HERE:** if Tesla ships DRIVER-token config creation, the next push succeeds, the member stops being produced, and no consumer changes. **TWO DIVERGENCES CLOSED, both by the contract rather than by the server. DV-24 RESOLVED:** v0.40.0 corrects the sentence that asserted §7.23 answers `404` on an ownership mismatch — it now states that §7.23 distinguishes `403 vehicle_not_owned` from `404`, that §7.29 collapses both to `404` so it cannot be an existence oracle, and that a client MUST NOT treat the two as interchangeable. **DV-25 RESOLVED:** v0.40.0 renumbers every §7.24 citation of the acknowledge endpoint to **§7.29**; §7.24–§7.28 were never renumbered, exactly as DV-25 said they must not be. **Sections updated in this document:** §1 TOC, §7.0 (`setupState` members + the new member's prose), §7.1 (`setupState` members, the precedence sentence, the full new-member entry with its evidence rule and upstream caveat), §7.23 (the enum row and the read-surface member-set paragraph), §7.29 (the numbering banner and note, the anchored line, the DV-24 note, the answer row), §10 (DV-24 and DV-25 both **RESOLVED**). Lockstep: `schemas/vehicle-summary.schema.json`, `schemas/vehicle-state.schema.json`, `schemas/vehicle-setup-completion.schema.json` (**re-vendored at v0.40.0**), `specs/rest.openapi.yaml` (`VehicleSummary.teslaAccessType` NEW and the `setupState.state` enum, BOTH members — v0.39.0 never reached it either), `data-classification.md` §1.19 (the `last_outcome` label list), and [`vehicle-state-schema.md`](vehicle-state-schema.md) §1.1 / §2.5 / §4 — **which is itself a drift fix**: v0.39.0's `teslaAccessType` and `awaiting_owner_acknowledgment` never reached that document, so it is now added to this endpoint family's Lockstep list rather than being remembered. | Claude (go-engineer) |
| 2026-09-05 | **A car you only DRIVE can be added, once you say its owner approved it ([MYR-599](https://linear.app/myrobotaxi/issue/MYR-599), CLIENT-DIRECTED).** Contracts **v0.39.0** — **one new OPTIONAL `VehicleSummary` / `VehicleState` field, one new `setupState` member, one new endpoint, one Go-owned migration, one new audit action, no new error code.** **THE FILTER WAS SILENT BY DESIGN AND THE SILENCE WAS THE BUG.** [MYR-257](https://linear.app/myrobotaxi/issue/MYR-257) finding 3 dropped every Fleet-API vehicle whose `access_type` was not `OWNER` with an `owner_vehicle_skipped reason=not_owner` line; on 2026-09-05 a tester linked a car he drives on somebody else's Tesla account, completed OAuth, stored a token and paired a virtual key, and got **no `Vehicle` row and no explanation**. The filter conflated two protections: *don't attach a car this person has no relationship with* (already guaranteed by the token-scoped fleet listing and `UpsertOwnedVehicle`'s cross-user rule, neither of which reads `access_type`) with *don't ACT on a car this person does not own* — which is real, and whose answer is **consent, not absence**. **The client's ruling (Thomas, 2026-09-05): the driver may add the car, behind a pop-up acknowledging that the owner approved it.** So the car IS provisioned and **NOTHING is pushed at it** — not at link time, not by the reconciler, not by complete-setup, reconnect or a fleet-config re-push — until the acknowledgment is recorded. **NEW `teslaAccessType` (§7.0 + §7.1, BOTH roles, P0):** `"owner"` \| `"driver"`, Tesla's open `access_type` narrowed to the two values the platform acts on, with **every** non-`OWNER` answer including an EMPTY one folding to `"driver"` (fail closed — an unknown access level is never promoted to ownership) and the raw token staying in the table for the operator question. **ABSENT reads as `"owner"`, and so does an unrecognised value** — absence is a positive `"owner"` by construction, because a pre-v0.39.0 server provisioned owner-access cars only. It is NOT the sibling `role`: `role` says whether the CALLER owns the platform's record, this says what TESLA thinks of the linking account, and `role: "owner"` + `teslaAccessType: "driver"` is exactly the row the field exists for. Delivery is REST-read-time only, like `role` / `rideShareEnabled` / `setupState`. **NEW `setupState` member `awaiting_owner_acknowledgment`, and it SORTS BEFORE the other three** — not a preference: no config push has been ATTEMPTED at such a car, so `awaiting_virtual_key` / `configuring` / `token_failed` (all three of which are claims ABOUT a push) cannot truthfully apply, and consent precedes pairing evidence in any case. Its `since` is when the driver-access row was recorded. It is also the only arm needing no `go_fleet_config_attempts` row, so it is evaluated ahead of the "no row ⇒ no claim" short-circuit. **NEW ENDPOINT `POST /api/tesla/vehicles/{vehicleId}/acknowledge-owner-approval`**, documented at **§7.29** — the contracts package cites it as §7.24, which has been the MYR-540 group-ride join since 2026-08-13 (**DV-25**; the path is the contract, the section number is an index into this file, and the vendored schemas are deliberately left byte-identical). Strict body `{"acknowledgmentVersion": "<1–64 chars>"}`, `additionalProperties: false`; **the server does NOT validate the id against a list of known versions** — an unrecognised id is recorded as sent, because a client shipped before a copy revision must not be blocked from finishing setup. Canonical id `owner-approval-v1`. **OWNERSHIP FAILURE IS `404`, NEVER `403`, deliberately unlike §7.23 / §7.15 / §7.12**: this endpoint records a consent about somebody else's property and must not be usable to probe which vehicleIds exist. Contracts v0.39.0's schema text asserts §7.23 also answers `404`; **it does not** — that is catalogued as **DV-24**, and §7.23's `403` is not changed. **THE FIRST ACKNOWLEDGMENT WINS**: `acknowledged_at` + `acknowledgment_version` are written only if not already set, because that first instant is what the platform would point to if an owner complained; a second call is **`200`, never `409`**, and re-runs the same best-effort push §7.23 performs. **An owner-access car is a `200` NO-OP** — nothing recorded, no audit row (an audit trail of non-events is worse than useless in the one conversation it exists for), `setupState` per the normal derivation — so a client that cannot tell the two cases apart is never punished for asking. **Failure is never a state**, exactly as on §7.23. **WHAT IS RECORDED IS EVIDENCE, NOT PERMISSION:** Tesla exposes no API by which an owner's approval could be verified, so the platform holds the one thing it actually knows — this account, at this instant, was shown this version of this text and agreed. The client's ruling: after **four** days of owner silence, one warning push; after **five**, remove the car's fleet-telemetry config. **WHAT SUSPENSION TOUCHES IS ONE CALL** — `DELETE /api/1/vehicles/{vin}/fleet_telemetry_config`, the SAME call the §7.12 teardown already makes, reused rather than re-implemented. The OAuth grant, the virtual key, the `Vehicle` row, every share and every ride survive untouched, and that narrowness is not modesty: it is exactly what makes §7.28's re-connect a single call with no OAuth and no lock/unlock. **STRICTLY THE OWNER'S ACTIVITY (explicit client ruling), and it is the rule a later reader is most likely to "fix":** rider and viewer usage defers NOTHING. A shared car whose owner has been away five days is suspended while a rider is watching it. The enforcement is structural rather than conditional — the candidate query joins the activity table on `"Vehicle"."userId"` and nothing else, so there is no rider probe to disable. **A RIDE IN PROGRESS IS NOT SPECIAL-CASED, also the ruling.** Near-impossible and not quite, since a shared rider can start one. There is deliberately no ride probe; what was verified is that the ride does not BREAK — suspension publishes no ride event, cancels nothing, ends no Live Activity and writes no ride table. The resulting lag is always conservative — a present owner reads as slightly less recent than they are, and the response to "less recent" tops out at a warning a day before anything irreversible. **AN OWNER WE HAVE NEVER OBSERVED IS NOT AN INACTIVE OWNER:** the join is INNER, which makes "suspend the entire fleet on the first pass after deploy" unreachable by construction rather than by a guard. **THE FIELD IS ON A SIDE TABLE AND COULD NOT HAVE BEEN A COLUMN.** CG-DL-9 forbids a Go migration from naming a Prisma-owned table at all, so `telemetrySuspendedAt` reads from Go-owned `go_vehicle_telemetry_suspensions` (migration **0044**) through a LEFT JOIN, composed by constant into all three §7.0 catalog queries. **Emitted on BOTH roles**, and the viewer arm is the one that needed arguing: a viewer who is not told renders a permanent spinner over a car that will never stream again, which the field spec forbids outright — a client can only obey a rule it has the input for, and the suspension is inferable from the silence anyway. IS NOT NULL`, so a row showing a name while the gate calls the owner nameless is not a bug that can be introduced. This is the CORRECTION to `label`, not a duplicate: `label` is the owner's own memo, typed before anybody redeemed anything and never resolved against an account, so a forwarded code left an accepted row naming the wrong person and the owner's Share tab could not say who actually holds the grant — the one question they are answering when they decide to revoke. Omitted on pending rows and on accepted rows with no resolvable name, deliberately INDISTINGUISHABLE because `status` already separates them. Owner-only by construction (the viewer role has no entry in the Invite mask resource at all — a viewer must never enumerate who else an owner shared with). **(4) FIX — `PATCH /api/users/me` could not name an Apple-native account.** The endpoint shipped earlier the same day as a single `UPDATE "User"`, and Apple-native accounts have **no `"User"` row at all** (they live in `go_users` + `go_identity_apple`), so it answered `404` to **exactly the nameless population it exists for**. The writer now updates every ladder rung the account has a row on, in one transaction — because **PRECEDENCE, NOT EXISTENCE, DECIDES WHAT WINS**: writing only `go_users` would leave a stale Apple first-consent name one rung above it and every reader would go on serving the OLD name while the endpoint reported success. Whichever rung the `COALESCE` selects now carries the new name, so there is no precedence to reason about and nothing to change when a fifth reader appears. No row is ever CREATED (an `INSERT` into `go_users` for an id living in `"User"` would fork one human across two identity sources), no migration, no new deletion step, and `data-lifecycle.md` §1.4's profile-name carve-out entry records the widening (the Prisma arm is still exactly one column; the two additional arms are Go-owned). **The `404` arm's MEANING therefore changed** and is now much narrower: no row in `"User"` **or** `go_identity_apple` **or** `go_users` — an orphaned token, not a routine Apple account. A dedicated go-side name store read as a new rung 0 was considered and rejected as the LARGER change (migration + four SQL constants + a §7.6 deletion step + a retention entry). **Sections updated:** §1 ToC, §2.3 (`PATCH` has TWO uses now, not one), §4.1.1 (`vehicle_unavailable` four carriers → five; the `subCode` enum note on why this one declined a sub-code), §5.2.0 (`ownerFirstName`, both roles), §5.2.5 (`acceptedByName`, owner-only), §6 catalog, §7.0 field table, §7.5.2 (new field subsection + example body), §7.8 (create gate, accept backstop, both error lists, and the dispatch-time hold policy's third arm), **§7.26 NEW** (`PATCH /api/users/me` had no reference section at all — added, including the storage argument and the new `404`). `vehicle-summary.schema.json`, `vehicle-sharing.schema.json`, `specs/rest.openapi.yaml`, both §7.0 fixtures, and `data-classification.md` updated in lockstep — two new **derived-field** blockquotes (`VehicleSummary.ownerFirstName` beside §1.9's `requesterName`, whose ladder it reuses verbatim, and `ShareInvite.acceptedByName` in §1.15), a provenance note on the P1 `go_users.name` / `go_identity_apple.name` columns (§1.10/§1.11 — now writable by the caller), and a §6 audit-trail entry recording that the counts DO NOT move: no columns, no tier changes, no encryption-scope change (P0 157, P1 48, unchanged). | Claude (go-engineer) |

This is that gate. **THE MODEL:** every OPEN ride on a vehicle **occupies a window of ±45 minutes** around its ride instant — `scheduledFor` for a reservation, **now** for an active instant ride — and a reservation whose instant falls **strictly inside** one is refused. The accept layer is not redundant: pairs booked *before* this gate can still be mutually conflicting, and the active-instant arm is time-relative (a car idle at booking may be mid-ride at accept). **ERROR SHAPE: `409 vehicle_unavailable` with the NEW `subCode: time_conflict`** — no new top-level code, because this is precisely the capability refusal that code already carries (MYR-277 in-service/offline, MYR-266 busy, MYR-342 paused) and NOT `conflict`, which means an illegal lifecycle transition. The sub-code is required because those three siblings are conditions of the car **right now** (client says "try later") while this is a property of the **time the rider picked** (client returns them to the picker), and §4.1 forbids branching on the message. **P1 DISCIPLINE — the body names the WINDOW, never the other ride:** the conflicting instant (P0 operational timing, the same disclosure the MYR-316 refusal already makes) and, when the claim is only pending, that fact — and **no** id, rider, requesterName, pickup or dropoff, and no `activeRideRequest`-style sibling object. The caller is not a party to that ride; a booking probe must not become a way to enumerate a stranger's calendar. Three messages, each true: `Vehicle is already booked for a ride at <RFC3339>`, `Vehicle already has a ride request for <RFC3339>` (pending), `Vehicle is already on a ride and can't also be booked for that time` (active instant, no instant to name). **`requested` COUNTS ON CREATE, NOT ON ACCEPT — deliberate, in ONE predicate behind one flag.** A pending reservation is a CLAIM on a slot but not a COMMITMENT of the car: create must not hand a rider a booking that will collide with somebody's pending request, while an owner's accept is precisely HOW a contested slot is decided — counting the peer there would refuse BOTH sides of a legacy double-booking and leave the owner unable to confirm either (the same stranding, from the other side), and would call a slot "booked" that nobody has booked. **MYR-313 NARROWED, PRECISELY:** its exemption covers the **status/availability gate only** (a reservation still accepts fine for an `in_service`/`offline` car — unchanged). The service-window bound (MYR-316), the pause (MYR-342) and now this window gate all **do** apply to reservations, because they ask about the reservation *instant* rather than the car *today*; §4.1.1's "scheduled rides are exempt" is therefore about (a)+(b), never about `vehicle_unavailable` as a whole, and the catalog row now says so. **RACE CONSTRUCTION: a per-vehicle ADVISORY TRANSACTION LOCK, not an index** — `BEGIN; pg_advisory_xact_lock(<vehicle>); <probe>; <INSERT|guarded UPDATE>; COMMIT`, so two conflicting bookings serialize and the loser's probe sees the winner's commit. Every value the link carries is covered by the one signature, including BOTH display names, so somebody holding a genuine link cannot rewrite `from` to a name the recipient would trust. Names are reduced server-side to the **first whitespace token, ASCII letters only, capped at 20**, and the parameter is **omitted entirely** when nothing survives (accented and non-Latin names lose characters or drop out; consumers render generic copy, never a placeholder built from the code). The signed expiry is the row's **actual `expires_at`** in unix seconds — the same value the redeem predicate reads — not a re-derived TTL. **The signature does not mean the invite is live**: redemption (§7.5.5) stays the only authority, and a resend **re-signs** with the new code, the new expiry, and the current names, so the previous link dies with the code it embeds. The one-character **key id** in `k` is the rotation seam: the shell holds `1` and `2` at once while links signed under `1` age out over their 7 days. `shareUrl` is **P1 and bearer** exactly as `code` is (it contains it) and is listed in `inviteOwnerFields`; **no new persisted column** — the URL is derived per request, so `data-classification.md` §1.15 is unchanged. | Claude |

One shared resolver (`internal/telemetry/service_window.go`) serves the snapshot, the list, and the scheduler bound, so three readers cannot drift. **`null` is COMMON AND NORMAL, not a failure:** every field of Tesla's `service_data` response is nullable and an ALL-NULL body is the ordinary shape for a visit with no appointment record — it is not an error, not a fetch failure, and not a claim that the car is back. **Tesla read piggybacks, it does not poll:** it fires on the ServiceStatusMonitor's existing connectivity-edge path for an `in_service` vehicle, sharing the SAME per-VIN read debounce (`defaultServiceReadCooldown`, 45s) as the existing `GET /api/1/vehicles/{vin}` edge read and the MYR-260 `/vehicle_data` backfill, and reusing the token that read already resolved; non-fatal on error, leaving the last-known estimate. **New §7.16 `PUT /api/tesla/vehicles/{vehicleId}/service-window`** (body `{"expectedEndAt":"<RFC3339>"}`), owner-only: **four accepted spellings CLEAR** — absent key, explicit `null`, empty/whitespace string, empty body — and the value MUST be in the FUTURE, else `400 invalid_request` `expectedEndAt must be in the future` (a malformed timestamp gives `expectedEndAt must be an RFC 3339 date-time`). Ownership semantics are byte-identical to §7.12/§7.14 (unknown → `404 not_found`, indistinguishable from ownership-filtered; mismatch → `403 vehicle_not_owned`), non-`PUT` → `405 invalid_request`, store failure → `500 internal_error`. **That ownership check is load-bearing in a way §7.14's is not:** the plate `UPDATE` re-scopes `WHERE "userId" = <caller>` as a second enforcement, but the side table has **no `userId` column** (CG-DL-9, no Prisma FKs), so there is no owner-scoped SQL predicate to fall back on. The `200` body `{"vehicleId":"…","expectedEndAt":"…" or null}` echoes the **OWNER column, not the resolved `serviceEstimatedEndAt`** — echoing the resolved value would tell a client its write was overruled when it was merely outranked by Tesla on the next read. **Scheduler bound (create AND accept):** `POST /api/ride-requests` and `POST /api/ride-requests/{id}/accept` refuse a `scheduledFor` EARLIER than the vehicle's current `serviceEstimatedEndAt` with **`400 invalid_request`** — **no new error code**, and not a `409`: a reservation for a time the car provably cannot serve is a bad *request*, not an illegal transition or a capability conflict — message `scheduledFor must not be earlier than the vehicle's estimated service end (<RFC3339>)`. **Three rules:** a **null estimate ⇒ NO BOUND** (scheduling stays fully open; neither consumers nor the server may ever block on missing data), **EQUAL is ALLOWED** (strictly "earlier than"), and **INSTANT rides are unaffected** (no `scheduledFor` to compare; already gated by MYR-277's in-service `409 vehicle_unavailable`). **MYR-313 interaction, stated explicitly:** a scheduled ACCEPT now **does** read the vehicle, where [MYR-313](https://linear.app/myrobotaxi/issue/MYR-313) short-circuited before the read — but that read **FAILS OPEN for scheduled rides** (an unreadable vehicle leaves the reservation UNBOUNDED rather than refused), the exact inverse of the instant path's fail-closed `500`, so the MYR-313 stranding defect cannot return; MYR-313's exemption from the AVAILABILITY gate is **unchanged** (in_service/offline scheduled accepts still succeed). **[SUPERSEDED by MYR-372, 2026-08-02 — that read now fails CLOSED. See the newest row and §7.8; this clause is retained as the record of what shipped on this date.]** **RBAC — BOTH roles**, on `vehicleStateOwnerFields` AND `vehicleSummaryOwnerFields` in `internal/mask/tables.go` (viewer inherits by the existing `removeField` derivation): a rider needs the window for the same reason the owner does — it floors the picker, so withholding it would break the one consumer it was built for. **Delivery: NOT STREAMED** — Tesla has no proto for a service ETC, so there is no `fieldMap` entry, **no fleet-config change**, and a `vehicle_update` frame NEVER carries `serviceEstimatedEndAt`; it is snapshot/list-only and lands on the next §7.0 / §7.1 read. §7.16 added; §7 index + §6 catalog rows added; §7.0 + §7.1 field tables, examples and RBAC lines, the §7.1 blockquote notes, §5.2.0 / §5.2.1 mask matrices, §7.8 create + accept error lines, the accept bound + MYR-313 paragraphs, the transition-matrix bullet, and the §4.1.1.b emission audit all updated; `schemas/vehicle-state.schema.json` (before `lastUpdated`) + `schemas/vehicle-summary.schema.json`, the OpenAPI `VehicleSummary` component, `data-classification.md` §1.13 (two columns + note), `vehicle-state-schema.md` §1.1/§2.4/§4, and the `snapshot`/`vehicles_list*`/`snapshot_completeness` fixtures updated. | 2026-07-28 | **On-demand state refresh — new §7.15 owner endpoint ([MYR-315](https://linear.app/myrobotaxi/issue/MYR-315)).** New `POST /api/tesla/vehicles/{vehicleId}/refresh` (no body), the **pull half of an otherwise entirely push-based read surface**: the WebSocket carries only what the car volunteers, and an asleep / in-service / merely quiet car volunteers nothing, so §7.1 keeps returning the last frame it ever saw while the MYR-260 backfills — which fire on *connectivity edges* — never trigger for a car that simply sits parked. Without this endpoint a user looking at stale data has no action available at all. **Three-rung ladder, in order.** (1) **Freshness short-circuit:** a LIVE streamed frame inside the **120 s** MYR-300 stream-authoritative window answers `200 {"status":"fresh","lastUpdated":"<last frame>"}` with **zero Tesla calls and no cooldown consumed** — refreshing already-current data would only cost the owner battery, and a healthy car must never be rate-limited for being healthy. (2) **Cooldown:** otherwise one Tesla-hitting refresh per vehicle per **60 s**, else `429 rate_limited` + `Retry-After: 60`. (3) **Wake + ONE read:** wake under the **same bounded budget vehicle commands use** (§7.9 — 3 attempts, 2 s backoff) via the new `commands.Executor.EnsureAwake`, which shares `wakeStep` with `Execute`'s asleep branch so the two can never drift; **probe-first**, so an *online but quiet* car (the common case) costs one cheap `GET /api/1/vehicles/{vin}` and **no wake at all**; then exactly ONE `vehicle_data` read republished through the **existing MYR-260 mapping** so values land on the identical broadcast + persist path a streamed frame takes and live clients see an ordinary `vehicle_update`. | 2026-07-27 | **Reservation-time dispatch — a scheduled ride's pickup nav now fires at `scheduledFor`, not at accept ([MYR-179](https://linear.app/myrobotaxi/issue/MYR-179)).** v1 changes only **WHEN** the existing leg-1 (pickup) push runs. **No new lifecycle status, no new wire field and no wire-shape change** — the MYR-176 latch columns (`dispatch_status`/`dispatched_at`/`dispatch_error`) are reused unchanged; the only schema work is **migration 0016**, a partial index (no columns, no constraints). **Accept half:** the nav-dispatch pipeline no longer pushes when the accepted ride carries `scheduledFor`; it returns without touching the latch, leaving the row latch-unclaimed and outcome-absent (deliberately NOT `skipped` — that is the kill-switch outcome and would both misreport the ride and latch it out of the sweep). Observable on the wire as `dispatchStatus`/`dispatchedAt` staying **absent** after a scheduled accept until the reservation instant. **Instant accepts are unchanged.** **Sweeper half:** a new `internal/dispatch` `ReservationSweeper` ticks every 30 s over `scheduled_for IS NOT NULL AND status = 'accepted' AND dispatched_at IS NULL AND scheduled_for <= now` (oldest first, `LIMIT 25`; the sweeper's own clock is passed into the query rather than using `NOW()` so ONE clock governs both due-selection and the lateness deadline), then hands each candidate to its OWN small worker pool (2), where the **same** `dispatched_at` latch is claimed and the **same** push pipeline runs via a `runLeg` → claim + `runClaimedLeg` split. The pass itself claims **nothing**: the latch is stamped JUST IN TIME, inside the worker after the busy re-check and immediately before the push, so claim → outcome is bounded by the per-dispatch `OverallTimeout` and stays under the startup reconciler's 5-minute floor — a deploy mid-pass hands unreached candidates back rather than burning them. The sweeper's pool is separate from the dispatcher's, so a reservation backlog can never delay an instant accept's push (**instant dispatch behaviour is unchanged under any reservation load**). Reuse is the design: **exactly-once across replicas** (the latch admits one winner, so every server may sweep with no coordination) and **crash safety** come for free — a crash between claim and outcome leaves the identical `dispatched_at` set / `dispatch_status` NULL orphan the **existing leg-1 startup reconciler** already resolves; its query filters on the latch columns only and has never mentioned `scheduled_for`, so scheduled rows were already in scope and **it required no widening** (now pinned by a store test). **Lateness ceiling (30 min)** — evaluated FIRST, before the vehicle is even consulted: a reservation still undispatched past `scheduledFor + 30 min` is **claimed and failed honestly** `failed` / new internal code **`reservation_expired`**, without a push, whatever the car is doing. That covers both causes (car busy the whole window, and dispatch itself unavailable after downtime or a kill-switch window) with one code, and stops a stale reservation from dialling a car hours late — the MYR-176 "an honest, alertable outcome beats a late nav push" stance applied to the sweeper. The deadline is anchored on `scheduledFor`, so a restart mid-hold resumes rather than resets it and downtime buys no fresh window. **Vehicle-busy hold** — the reservation-time availability re-check MYR-313 deferred here: inside the ceiling and immediately before claiming, the worker tests the per-vehicle busy predicate (`scheduled_for IS NULL AND status IN ('accepted','arrived','enroute')`, character-for-character `uq_go_ride_requests_active_instant_vehicle` and now SHARED in code with the `hasActiveRide` catalog flag so a third reader cannot drift). Busy → **hold** (no claim, no outcome, no push; retried next tick, so the ride dispatches the moment the car frees up); busy state unreadable → hold, never claim. Held rows are also filtered out of the selection window in SQL so they cannot head-of-line block younger dispatchable reservations out of the `LIMIT`, while past-ceiling rows are exempt from that filter and always surface for resolution. **Claim-time re-validation** — the reservation claim is its own guarded `UPDATE` re-checking `status = 'accepted' AND scheduled_for IS NOT NULL`, so a rider cancel or an owner picked-up landing between the sweep's SELECT and the claim LOSES: no push, no outcome, no event. The instant path's claim is deliberately left unguarded and byte-identical to MYR-176. **New internal `ride.due` seam** (`events.RideDueEvent`, ids + `scheduledFor` + `dueAt`): published once per due ride, and only when the push actually resolved **`sent`** — the topic means "your car is on the way", so kill-switched (`skipped`), token-failed, command-failed and expired reservations emit nothing (the latch admits one winner, so a false event could never be corrected). Internal-only (never broadcast, no REST surface), fire-and-forget and drop-safe, **no consumer yet** — a hook for the planned rider push notification. **New kill-switch `RESERVATION_DISPATCH_ENABLED`** (default true, `strconv.ParseBool` fail-fast like `DISPATCH_ENABLED`): false stops the sweeper entirely, leaving reservations unclaimed so re-enabling picks them up rather than having burned them; `DISPATCH_ENABLED=false` still records due reservations `skipped` exactly like instant accepts. **Indexing:** migration 0016 adds `idx_go_ride_requests_reservation_due`, a partial index over `scheduled_for` whose predicate is exactly the sweep query's three static conjuncts, so the every-30s pass on every replica stays an index probe as `go_ride_requests` accumulates terminal rows forever. **Accept-after-due:** `scheduledFor` is not floored to the future, so a reservation accepted after its instant dispatches on the next tick while inside the 30-minute ceiling and resolves `reservation_expired` beyond it — now documented. **v1 boundaries (both directions):** the busy predicate excludes scheduled rides (mirroring the index), so two reservations for one car at overlapping times both dispatch; and the model is one-directional — a car mid-RESERVATION is not busy to the instant path, so an instant accept can still re-point it. Both belong to booking-time conflict detection / an accept-side guard, not dispatch. §7.8 accept section, new "Reservation-time dispatch" subsection, `dispatch_error` code list, and transition-matrix note updated.
